Multiclass Classification

Our dataset consists of clinical data from patients who entered the hospital complaining of chest pain (“angina”) during exercise. The information collected includes:

  • age : Age of the patient

  • sex : Sex of the patient

  • cp : Chest Pain type

    • Value 0: asymptomatic
    • Value 1: typical angina
    • Value 2: atypical angina
    • Value 3: non-anginal pain

  • trtbps : resting blood pressure (in mm Hg)

  • chol : cholesterol in mg/dl fetched via BMI sensor

  • restecg : resting electrocardiographic results

    • Value 0: normal
    • Value 1: having ST-T wave abnormality (T wave inversions and/or ST elevation or depression of > 0.05 mV)
    • Value 2: showing probable or definite left ventricular hypertrophy by Estes’ criteria

  • thalach : maximum heart rate achieved during exercise

  • output : the doctor’s diagnosis of whether the patient is at risk for a heart attack

    • 0 = not at risk of heart attack
    • 1 = at risk of heart attack
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from io import StringIO
from IPython.display import display
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold, cross_val_predict, cross_val_score
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score, f1_score, classification_report

predictors = ["trtbps", "chol", "age"]
cv = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)

def logistic_model():
    return Pipeline([
        ("scale", StandardScaler()),
        ("model", LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=42))
    ])

def plot_predictions(frame, predicted, title, labels):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    colors = plt.get_cmap("tab10")
    predicted = np.asarray(predicted).astype(str)
    for j, (value, label) in enumerate(labels.items()):
        selected = predicted == str(value)
        ax.scatter(frame.loc[selected, "trtbps"], frame.loc[selected, "chol"],
                   s=frame.loc[selected, "age"] * 1.6, alpha=0.55,
                   color=colors(j), label=label)
    ax.set(xlabel="Resting blood pressure (mm Hg)", ylabel="Cholesterol (mg/dL)", title=title)
    ax.legend(title="Class; point size = age", loc="best")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

How the models are checked: I use resting blood pressure, cholesterol, and age for every model. Test estimates come from five stratified folds with a fixed seed of 42. Scaling is fitted inside each training fold to avoid data leakage. The probability tables and plots use the full training data; the reported scores use held-out predictions. For accuracy, precision, recall, and F1, I combine the held-out predictions across the five folds. For ROC-AUC, I report the mean of the five test-fold AUCs. Logistic regression uses the usual 0.5 cutoff. Macro scores give each class equal weight. All scores are on a 0–1 scale.

Q1: A Natural Multiclass Model: k-nearest neighbors

Fit a multiclass 10-nearest neighbors model. Output the predicted class probabilities and plot the predicted classes for the training data. Estimate the test:

  • accuracy
  • macro precision, recall, and F1 scores
  • precision, recall, and F1 score for each class. You will likely get some weird values; can you explain why?
knn = Pipeline([
    ("scale", StandardScaler()),
    ("model", KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=10))
])
knn.fit(X, y)

# These probabilities and the plot describe the fitted training data.
knn_probabilities = pd.DataFrame(
    knn.predict_proba(X), columns=[f"P(cp={k})" for k in knn.classes_], index=ha.index
)
print("Q1: Predicted training probabilities (all patients stored in knn_probabilities)")
display(knn_probabilities)
plot_predictions(ha, knn.predict(X), "10-NN: predicted training classes", {str(k): str(k) for k in range(4)})

# Each patient is predicted by a model trained on the other four folds.
knn_oof = cross_val_predict(knn, X, y, cv=cv, method="predict")
q1_metrics = pd.Series({
    "Accuracy": accuracy_score(y, knn_oof),
    "Macro precision": precision_score(y, knn_oof, average="macro", zero_division=0),
    "Macro recall": recall_score(y, knn_oof, average="macro", zero_division=0),
    "Macro F1": f1_score(y, knn_oof, average="macro", zero_division=0)
}, name="Out-of-fold test estimate")
print("Q1 ANSWER: Estimated test performance")
display(q1_metrics.to_frame().round(4))
q1_report = pd.DataFrame(classification_report(
    y, knn_oof, labels=["0", "1", "2", "3"], output_dict=True, zero_division=0
)).T
print("Q1 ANSWER: Precision, recall, F1, and support for each class")
display(q1_report.loc[["0", "1", "2", "3"]].round(4))
print("Out-of-fold predicted class counts:")
display(pd.Series(knn_oof).value_counts().reindex(["0", "1", "2", "3"], fill_value=0))

Q1 Answer: The estimated test accuracy is 0.4103. Macro precision is 0.2105, macro recall is 0.2375, and macro F1 is 0.2047. The table above gives the scores for each class. The classes are uneven: class 0 has 128 patients, class 1 has 44, class 2 has 81, and class 3 has only 20. With 10 neighbors, a rare class can lose the vote to more common classes, especially when the predictors overlap. If a class is never predicted, its precision is undefined because there are no predicted positives. I report it as 0 using zero_division=0. Its recall and F1 are also 0 when none of its actual cases are identified. These zero scores do not mean the class is missing from the data.

Q2: OvR for Class 3

Fit a logistic regression model for predicting Class 3. Output the predicted class probabilities (Class 3 or not) and plot the predicted classes (Class 3 or not) for the training data. Estimate the test:

  • precision, recall, and F1 score for class 3
def fit_ovr(category):
    target = ha[f"cp_is_{category}"]
    model = logistic_model()
    model.fit(X, target)
    probabilities = pd.DataFrame(
        model.predict_proba(X),
        columns=[f"P(not {category})", f"P(class {category})"], index=ha.index
    )
    print(f"Class {category}: predicted training probabilities")
    display(probabilities)
    plot_predictions(ha, model.predict(X), f"Logistic OvR: class {category} vs. rest (training)",
                     {0: f"Not {category}", 1: f"Class {category}"})
    predicted = cross_val_predict(model, X, target, cv=cv, method="predict")
    metrics = {
        "Class": str(category),
        "Precision": precision_score(target, predicted, pos_label=1, zero_division=0),
        "Recall": recall_score(target, predicted, pos_label=1, zero_division=0),
        "F1": f1_score(target, predicted, pos_label=1, zero_division=0),
        "Actual positives": int(target.sum()),
        "Predicted positives": int(predicted.sum())
    }
    return model, probabilities, metrics

ovr_models, ovr_probabilities, ovr_metrics = {}, {}, {}
ovr_models[3], ovr_probabilities[3], ovr_metrics[3] = fit_ovr(3)
print("Q2 ANSWER: Class 3 estimated test scores")
display(pd.DataFrame([ovr_metrics[3]]).set_index("Class").round(4))

    ovr_models[category], ovr_probabilities[category], ovr_metrics[category] = fit_ovr(category)

Q4: OvO

Reduce your dataset to only the 0 and 1 types of chest pain.

Then, fit a Logistic Regression to predict between the two groups, and estimate the ROC-AUC.

def compare_pair(other):
    pair = ha.loc[ha["cp"].isin(["0", str(other)])].copy()
    pair_X = pair[predictors]
    # The nonzero category is the positive class for ROC-AUC.
    pair_y = (pair["cp"] == str(other)).astype(int)
    model = logistic_model()
    aucs = cross_val_score(model, pair_X, pair_y, cv=cv, scoring="roc_auc")
    model.fit(pair_X, pair_y)
    result = {
        "Pair": f"0 vs {other}", "Patients": len(pair),
        "Mean test ROC-AUC": aucs.mean(), "Fold SD": aucs.std(ddof=1)
    }
    return model, result, aucs

ovo_models, ovo_metrics, ovo_fold_aucs = {}, {}, {}
ovo_models[1], ovo_metrics[1], ovo_fold_aucs[1] = compare_pair(1)
print("Q4 ANSWER: Class 0 vs. class 1")
display(pd.DataFrame([ovo_metrics[1]]).set_index("Pair").round(4))
print("ROC-AUC by test fold:", np.round(ovo_fold_aucs[1], 4))
